title: Business: Mindset and Leadership
coreMove: Leadership mindset becomes culture: people either hide problems to protect status or surface them early enough to learn, coach, and adapt.

exampleSpecs.audience: analysts deciding whether to surface bad news
exampleSpecs.stakes: a concealed exposure could become a company crisis
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Enron to show talent worship turning image protection into risk

exampleSpecs.audience: new managers receiving blunt performance feedback
exampleSpecs.stakes: the group may defend poor decisions instead of improving
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Wood and Bandura to show fixed managers treating feedback as judgment

exampleSpecs.domain: nonprofit board review after a failed campaign
exampleSpecs.stakes: donors and staff may lose trust if critique is buried
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Lee Iacocca and peer executive examples to show leader image distorting company judgment

exampleSpecs.stakes: cuts could become domination rather than disciplined change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Welch, Gerstner, and Mulcahy to show growth leadership as tough listening and development

exampleSpecs.stakes: silent disagreement could push a bad launch forward
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Bay of Pigs groupthink to make dissent surface before consensus hardens

exampleSpecs.stakes: patient wait times may worsen if leaders soften the data
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Jim Collins good-to-great findings to pair brutal facts with belief in improvement
